title: Proximity-Induced Giant Majorana Spin Response in a UTe$_2$-Metal Film Heterostructure
authors: Jushin Tei, Makoto Shimizu, Yukio Tanaka, Satoshi Fujimoto, Takeshi Mizushima
abstract: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe$_2$ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional $p$-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.
summary: This theoretical work proposes using the superconducting proximity effect in a UTe2/Metal heterostructure to detect Majorana surface states. By measuring the enhanced Ising-anisotropic spin response via NMR, the authors provide a robust, symmetry-sensitive diagnostic tool. The key finding is that this signature persists even when the interface coupling is weak, making the detection scheme highly practical.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish an experimentally accessible method to identify Majorana surface states (MSSs) by probing their intrinsic Ising spin response.
main_result: The superconducting proximity effect transfers Majorana correlations into an adjacent metal film, leading to a giant, symmetry-protected Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate, which is robust even in the tunneling regime.
method: Theoretical modeling using anomalous Green's functions and Dyson equations to calculate spin-lattice relaxation rates and static susceptibilities.
model_or_system: The system is a UTe2 superconductor coupled to a normal metal film on the (100) surface. The theory models the proximity-induced odd-frequency spin-triplet correlations.
key_observables: Spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T1T), static spin susceptibility ($\chi_\alpha$), and the Ising-anisotropic spin response ($R_\alpha$).
important_parameters: Impurity scattering rate ($\gamma_{	ext{imp}}$), proximity coupling strength ($\lambda$), and interface transparency ($T$). The analysis focuses on the diffusive regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the neglect of lattice mismatch and interfacial reconstruction, and uses approximations like the self-consistent Born approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial/frequency dependence of induced pair amplitudes, and show the temperature dependence of the Majorana spin response ($R_\alpha(T)$) in both clean and diffusive limits, demonstrating enhancement factors.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the proximity effect, then calculating the response in the diffusive limit, and finally demonstrating the robustness of the Ising enhancement across varying interface transparencies (tunneling regime).
why_interesting: The focus on spin response, symmetry protection, and the use of proximity effects to make surface phenomena measurable via bulk techniques (NMR) is highly relevant to open quantum systems and superconducting interfaces.

Because the B3u state supports no Majorana surface states on the (100) surface, none of the spin components exhibits an enhancement.
